questions.question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

Educators play a __key __ role as nation builders.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (1)** i.e. **'negligible'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **In this context, the word 'key'** refers to the importance of education for nation-building.
 
• **Key: **(मुख्य) Of great importance, significance, or central to a particular situation.
 
 
• **Example:** Proper communication is **key** to successful teamwork.
 
 
 
• **Negligible: **(तुच्छ) So small or unimportant that it can be disregarded or considered insignificant.
 
 
• **Example:** It was silly to argue over such a **negligible **amount of money.
 
 
 
• Hence it is clear that negligible is the antonym of Key.

*Therefore, the correct answer is* ***'negligible'.*** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Principal: **(मुख्य) The most important or leading person or thing in a particular situation.

 
 
• **Example: **The principal reason for the delay was the heavy traffic.
 
 
 
• **Primitive:** (प्राचीन) Relating to an early stage of development or an early form of something.
 
 
• **Example:** The tools and weapons used by ancient civilizations were often primitive.
 
 
 
• **Predominant:** (प्रमुख) Having control, influence, or authority over others.
 
 
• **Example: **In tropical rainforests, the predominant plant life consists of various species of trees.

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The differences were/ imperceptible to all but/ the most trained eye.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e.** 'No error'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Let's check all the segments of the given statement:

 
• **'The differences were'**: The subject **'differences'** is plural so the verb **'were'** is plural.
 
• **'imperceptible to all but'**: "To all but" is a phrase meaning "to everyone except." It’s correctly used here.
 
• **'the most trained eye'**: Here the use of **'the'** is correct because we use the before superlative degree. The word **'trained'** used as a participle is also apt.
 
• So, the sentence is a **'no error' **construction.

**The correct sentence is**: The differences were imperceptible to all but the most trained eye.

questions.question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

We've made extraordinary (flowering as a) society in that regard.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e.** 'progress as a'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here the sentence wants to say we've made extraordinary **development or improvement** as a society.
 
• So, the correct answer should have a meaning that is similar to '**development or improvement'**.
 
• **Flowering** means *the action of producing flowers*.
 
 
• **For Example** - The clematis can be grown to coincide with the** flowering** of the roses
 
 
 
• So, this is not appropriate here.
 
• **Progress** means *development towards an improved or more advanced condition.*
 
 
• **For Example** - We are making **progress** towards equal rights
 
 
 
• So, the most appropriate phrase to replace the bracketed portion is **'progress as a'**.

 Therefore, the correct answer is: **'progress as a'.**

**The correct sentence is: **We've made extraordinary **progress as a__** society in that regard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's discuss the other options:
 
 
• **'Improvement by a'** is incorrect here because normally 'by' is used in the passive voice but the given sentence is in the active voice. 
 
• **'Advance as a'** is also not suitable in the context of the sentence.
 
• So, they are not appropriate to replace the bracketed portion.

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Even the most wise don't / know what's hidden in / the depths of their being.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (4)**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Even the most wise don't" **is the erroneous part. It should be written as **"Even the wisest don't".**
 
• **'wise'** is an adjective. An adjective has three degrees: (Positive-Comparative-Superlative).
 
• **'Wise'** has its own superlative form **'wisest'.**
 
• We use **'most'** before those adjectives which have no superlative form.
 
• **For example:** Beautiful. It has no superlative form. That's why most is added before it; "**Most beautiful".**
 
• The other segments of the given sentence have no errors.

Therefore, the correct sentence is ***"******Even the wisest don't /** know what's hidden in / the depths of their being**"**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__***

 
• **"The wisest" **is a plural noun. It refers to the whole wise community. That's why **'their'** is used as a pronoun of 'the wisest' in the given sentence.

 
 
• **For example: "The poor" **is also a plural noun. It refers to the whole poor community.

 
 
• The poor deserve access to quality education and healthcare.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

It is expected that this police power will only apply to air and (sea routes between the Great Britain and the Northern Ireland).

options.text: Sea routes across the Great Britain and Northern Ireland
Sea routes across the Great Britain and the Northern Ireland
Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e. **'Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The use of **'the'** before *Great Britain* and* Northern Ireland*, is wrong.
 
• **'The'** is used before the name of countries which are a group of islands or the country that contains a political title in its name.
 
 
• **For Example** - The Bahamas, The United Kingdom, The Czech Republic, etc.
 
 
 
• On the other hand names of the countries like India, **Northern Ireland**, **Great Britain**, etc. do not take **'the'** before them.
 
 
• For Example -
 
 
• I am from** the India** (**Not Correct**)
 
• I am from **India** (**Correct**)
 
 
 
 
 
• So, according to the rule, the correct form of the bracketed portion is **'****Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland'.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland'.**

**The correct sentence is:** It is expected that this police power will only apply to air and **sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland__**.

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

'He wants something done, / and it has not happen / fast enough,' he said.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (4)**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous segment is **“and it has not happen”.**
 
• This segment is in the ***present perfect tense***. Rule (**Subject + have/has +V3**)
 
• **‘happen’ **is the base form(V1) of verb. The past participle(V3) form of the verb is **‘happened’.**
 
• Hence, it should be written as** “and it has not happened”.**
 
 
• **For example: **He has completed his task.
 
 

Therefore, the correct sentence is *“He wants something done, **and it has not happened **fast enough,” he said.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

__
 
• The phrase **"something done"** is a way of expressing that a task or action needs to be completed without specifying the exact task.
 
• It's a general term used when someone wants a particular action to be taken care of, but they may not provide all the details about what that action is.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• It is a direct speech. 
 
• It is not necessary to change the tense which is under quotation.
 
• If we change it into indirect, we have to change it into past tense.
 
• In this context, no need to change it.

questions.question:

The event acts as a trigger or ________, which catapults them into an awareness of this phenomenon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (2)** i.e. **'catalyst'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence, using both **"trigger"** and **"catalyst"** emphasizes the idea that the event not only initiates a response but also actively accelerates their awareness of the phenomenon.

 
 
• **Trigger: **(किसी विशिष्ट क्रिया या प्रतिक्रिया का कारण बनना) To cause a specific action or reaction; a device that initiates a process.

 
 
• **Example: **The loud noise could ***trigger ***anxiety in some individuals.
 
 
 
• **Catalyst: **(संवेगक) Something that speeds up or facilitates a chemical reaction or a process.
 
 
• **Example:** The new technology acted as a ***catalyst ***for innovation in the industry.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the complete sentence is ***"****The event acts as a trigger or **catalyst**__, which catapults them into an awareness of this phenomenon**"**.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__ **

 
• **Dogma: **(सिद्धांत) A set of principles or beliefs that are accepted as an authoritative truth, often without question.

 
 
• **Example: **The religious group followed the ***dogma ***of their faith unwaveringly.
 
 
 
• **Elegy: **(शोकगीत) A poem or composition that mourns or laments the dead or reflects on something lost.
 
 
• **Example:** The poet wrote an ***elegy ***in memory of his late friend.
 
 
 
• **Harangue: **(उग्र या जोशीला भाषण देना) A lengthy and forceful speech, often critical or scolding in nature.
 
 
• **Example: **The politician delivered a ***harangue ***against government policies.
